name: Question 8
problem:
The displacement $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
r=⟨1-4{e}^{t/2},\,{e}^{4-t}⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the particle when $t=3\,\text{s}.$ Round your final answer to the nearest Newton.
worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate $r$ to get the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-4{e}^{t/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{4-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{e}^{t/2},\,-{e}^{4-t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{t/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{4-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{t/2},\,{e}^{4-t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =5\cdot ⟨-{e}^{t/2},\,{e}^{4-t}⟩ \\  & =⟨-5{e}^{t/2},\,5{e}^{4-t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=3\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(3) & =⟨-5{e}^{3/2},\,5{e}^{4-3}⟩ \\  & =⟨-5{e}^{3/2},\,5e⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of $F(3)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|F(3)| & =\sqrt{(-5{e}^{3/2})^{2}+{(5e)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25{e}^{3}+25{e}^{2}} \\  & =5e\sqrt{e+1} \\  & ≈26\,\text{N}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest Newton.

Question 8
?

The displacement r, in meters, of a particle P of mass 5kg is given by r=⟨1−4et/2,e4−t⟩, where t>0 is the time in seconds. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the particle when t=3s. Round your final answer to the nearest Newton.

a
29N
b
26N
c
14N
d
31N
e
18N
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Newton’s second law states that F=ma, where F is the resultant force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate r to get the velocity vector:

v=drdt=⟨ddt(1−4et/2),ddt(e4−t)⟩=⟨−2et/2,−e4−t⟩

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

a=dvdt=⟨ddt(−2et/2),ddt(−e4−t)⟩=⟨−et/2,e4−t⟩

Therefore, the resultant force F at time t equals

F=ma=5⋅⟨−et/2,e4−t⟩=⟨−5et/2,5e4−t⟩.

When t=3s, we have

F(3)=⟨−5e3/2,5e4−3⟩=⟨−5e3/2,5e⟩.

Finally, the magnitude of F(3) is given by

|F(3)|=(−5e3/2)2+(5e)2=25e3+25e2=5ee+1≈26N

rounded to the nearest Newton.
